# mongodump and mongorestore semantics: --oplog, --oplogReplay, namespace filters and sharded-cluster limits — facts

## Structure and components

- [statement] If the dump contains no data files matching --nsInclude, mongorestore restores no data for that requested namespace. (high confidence) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/database-tools/mongorestore.md · keywords: mongodump and mongorestore semantics: --oplog, --oplogReplay, namespace filters and sharded-cluster limits · also: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/database-tools/mongorestore/mongorestore-examples.md

## How it works

- [statement] For a replica-set backup, mongodump --oplog captures writes during the dump; mongorestore --oplogReplay applies the captured operations after restoring the data. Capture ends when mongodump finishes and does not cover later writes. A directory dump stores the captured operations in oplog.bson. (high confidence) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/database-tools/mongorestore/mongorestore-examples.md · keywords: mongodump and mongorestore semantics: --oplog, --oplogReplay, namespace filters and sharded-cluster limits · also: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/database-tools/mongodump.md, https://www.mongodb.com/docs/database-tools/mongorestore.md
- [statement] For a restore without oplog replay, --nsInclude selects matching namespaces and --nsExclude removes matching namespaces. Both accept asterisk patterns. Exclusion takes precedence when both match. The documented command selects transactions.* while excluding transactions.*_dev. (high confidence) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/database-tools/mongorestore.md · keywords: mongodump and mongorestore semantics: --oplog, --oplogReplay, namespace filters and sharded-cluster limits · also: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/database-tools/mongorestore/mongorestore-examples.md
- [statement] The --oplogLimit timestamp is an exclusive upper bound: mongorestore omits entries with timestamps greater than or equal to it. It requires --oplogReplay, and MongoDB warns that manually selecting oplog entries can cause corruption or inconsistencies. (low confidence) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/database-tools/mongorestore.md · keywords: mongodump and mongorestore semantics: --oplog, --oplogReplay, namespace filters and sharded-cluster limits

## How-to and procedures

- [statement] Use --nsFrom and --nsTo together to rename matching namespaces during restore. Each option requires its matching counterpart. (low confidence) — https://github.com/mongodb/mongo-tools/blob/master/mongorestore/options.go · keywords: mongodump and mongorestore semantics: --oplog, --oplogReplay, namespace filters and sharded-cluster limits
- [statement] To restore a sharded-cluster dump, the documented procedure stops balancing, creates and pre-shards destination collections with the source shard keys, restores through mongos while excluding config.*, and restarts balancing. Using --drop after pre-sharding removes the sharding configuration. (low confidence) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/tutorial/restore-sharded-cluster-with-database-dumps.md · keywords: mongodump and mongorestore semantics: --oplog, --oplogReplay, namespace filters and sharded-cluster limits
- [statement] Use --nsFrom with --nsTo to rename namespaces during restore. Asterisk replacements correspond linearly between the two patterns; dollar-delimited wildcard variables support nonlinear replacements. These options perform namespace renaming. (high confidence) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/database-tools/mongorestore.md · keywords: mongodump and mongorestore semantics: --oplog, --oplogReplay, namespace filters and sharded-cluster limits · also: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/database-tools/mongorestore/mongorestore-examples.md

## Facts and statements

- [statement] mongorestore --oplogReplay requires a full member dump created with mongodump --oplog. Do not combine it with --db, --collection, --nsInclude, --nsExclude, --nsFrom, or --nsTo. The implementation explicitly rejects includes, excludes, and namespace renames. The community thread also corrects a suggestion to use nsInclude with replay. (high confidence) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/database-tools/mongorestore.md · keywords: mongodump and mongorestore semantics: --oplog, --oplogReplay, namespace filters and sharded-cluster limits · also: https://github.com/mongodb/mongo-tools/blob/master/mongorestore/mongorestore.go, https://www.mongodb.com/community/forums/t/dump-and-restore-live-instance/197720
- [statement] Sharded clusters do not support mongorestore --oplogReplay. mongodump --oplog is not a supported way to capture a sharded-cluster backup through mongos; the mongodump reference says it has no effect there and directs users to the dedicated sharded procedure. (high confidence) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/database-tools/mongorestore.md · keywords: mongodump and mongorestore semantics: --oplog, --oplogReplay, namespace filters and sharded-cluster limits · also: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/database-tools/mongodump.md
- [statement] The documented sharded-cluster dump procedure requires stopping the balancer, writes, and schema transformations. It stops balancing, locks the cluster via mongos, takes the dump through mongos, then unlocks and restarts balancing; its consistency condition requires following the steps exactly with no operations in progress at the start. (low confidence) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/tutorial/backup-sharded-cluster-with-database-dumps.md · keywords: mongodump and mongorestore semantics: --oplog, --oplogReplay, namespace filters and sharded-cluster limits
- [statement] In its July 25, 2016 explanation, Percona identifies different shard backup completion times as a consistency problem: capturing each shard oplog only until its own dump finishes does not cover a common completion point. The article describes coordinating oplog recording until the last shard finishes; this historical explanation does not establish current support for replaying directly to a sharded cluster. (low confidence) — https://www.percona.com/blog/mongodb-consistent-backups/ · keywords: mongodump and mongorestore semantics: --oplog, --oplogReplay, namespace filters and sharded-cluster limits
- [statement] Without --oplog, a mongodump taken while writes continue does not represent a single moment in time. (low confidence) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/database-tools/mongodump.md · keywords: mongodump and mongorestore semantics: --oplog, --oplogReplay, namespace filters and sharded-cluster limits
- [statement] mongodump --excludeCollection and --excludeCollectionsWithPrefix require a database specified through --db or the URI; repeat either option to exclude multiple collection names or prefixes. (low confidence) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/database-tools/mongodump.md · keywords: mongodump and mongorestore semantics: --oplog, --oplogReplay, namespace filters and sharded-cluster limits
- [statement] mongodump --oplog fails if collection renames, aggregation with $out, mapReduce, user/role/privilege changes, or cluster-wide setting changes such as setDefaultRWConcern occur during the dump. (low confidence) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/database-tools/mongodump.md · keywords: mongodump and mongorestore semantics: --oplog, --oplogReplay, namespace filters and sharded-cluster limits
- [statement] The documented sharded-cluster dump procedure needs MongoDB support for fsync locking through mongos: MongoDB 7.1, or the backported releases 7.0.2, 6.0.11, and 5.0.22. (low confidence) — https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/tutorial/backup-sharded-cluster-with-database-dumps.md · keywords: mongodump and mongorestore semantics: --oplog, --oplogReplay, namespace filters and sharded-cluster limits
